As discussed in previous thread [1]
handing hugetlb migration.  When handling the migration of freed hugetlb
it prevents fallback to other NUMA nodes in
alloc_and_dissolve_hugetlb_folio().  However
hugetlb
column2: it allows fallback to other NUMA nodes in

column1: alloc_hugetlb_folio_nodemask()
column2: which can break the per-node hugetlb pool

column1: and might result in unexpected failures when node bound workloads doesn't
get what is asssumed available.
To make hugetlb migration strategy more clear
column2: we should list all the scenarios

column1: of hugetlb migration and analyze whether allocation fallback is permitted:
1) Memory offline: will call dissolve_free_huge_pages() to free the
freed hugetlb
column2: and call do_migrate_range() to migrate the in-use

column1: hugetlb.  Both can break the per-node hugetlb pool
explicit offlining operation
column2: no better choice.  So should allow the

column1: hugetlb allocation fallback.
2) Memory failure: same as memory offline.  Should allow fallback to a
different node might be the only option to handle it
impact of poisoned memory can be amplified.
3) Longterm pinning: will call migrate_longterm_unpinnable_pages() to
migrate in-use and not-longterm-pinnable hugetlb
per-node pool.  But we should fail to longterm pinning if can not
allocate on current node to avoid breaking the per-node pool.
4) Syscalls (mbind
users operation to move pages to other nodes
nodes should not be prohibited.
5) alloc_contig_range: used by CMA allocation and virtio-mem
fake-offline to allocate given range of pages.  Now the freed hugetlb
migration is not allowed to fallback
hugetlb migration should be also not allowed to fallback.
6) alloc_contig_pages: used by kfence
should be consistent with that of alloc_contig_range().
Based on the analysis of the various scenarios above
helper to determine whether fallback is permitted according to the
migration reason..
